name: message-test-002-family-history-headlines
question: How likely would you be to actually sign up and pay for this? Answer honestly as yourself, including any hesitations.

concepts.headline: Heart disease runs in your family. It doesn't have to run in you.
concepts.pitch: A board-certified physician baselines your ApoB, blood pressure, and coronary calcium score — then manages them down with you, by video and direct messaging. No insurance needed.

personas.description: 52-year-old male engineering manager in Troy, Michigan. Household income $145k, employer PPO with high deductible. Just got a coronary calcium score of 280 from a $75 hospital screening; his PCP said 'we'll keep an eye on it.' Analytical, reads studies, frustrated by 12-minute appointments. Has an HSA with $9k in it.

44-year-old female elementary school teacher in Grand Rapids, Michigan. Household income $98k, insured through the district. Her father died of a heart attack at 58 and her older brother just got a stent at 49. Scared but busy, skeptical of wellness fads, watches spending carefully.

38-year-old female HR coordinator in Warren, Michigan. Income $72k. Lost 48 pounds on compounded semaglutide; her telehealth provider just sent a transition notice and branded versions cost $349/month. Worried about regain and blood pressure creeping back. Was paying ~$200/month.

41-year-old male self-employed flooring contractor in Lansing, Michigan. Income varies $60-90k, no insurance, hasn't seen a doctor in 6 years. Knows his blood pressure ran high at a pharmacy machine. Price-sensitive, distrusts the system, wife pushing him to get checked.

35-year-old male software developer in Ann Arbor, Michigan. Income $165k, excellent insurance, longevity-podcast listener, pays $365/year for Function Health, wears a Whoop. Wants ApoB optimization and qualified interpretation; allergic to dumbed-down messaging.

58-year-old female retail worker in Flint, Michigan. Household income $52k, Marketplace bronze plan with $7k deductible. On lisinopril from an urgent-care visit, no regular doctor. $99/month feels like a lot; needs convincing it replaces existing costs.
